subject: Priv infra CI safety checklist and artifact provenance for AegisBank
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Priv infra CI safety checklist and artifact provenance for AegisBank

Team —

We're approaching the private deployment handoff for AegisBank next week (pilot in their VPC). Julie from Aegis asked specifically for: artifact provenance (signed builds), CI gating criteria for Terraform/Helm/Ansible modules, and a short evidence packet we can provide to their security team.

Attached is a first-pass checklist and a small pipeline diff that proposes an additional signing step and provenance metadata annotation. Priorities for this thread:

- Confirm the minimal gating checks that satisfy their compliance ask (SLSA-like provenance will suffice).
- Agree on where signed artifacts will be stored and the signing key management pattern (customer KMS vs. Redwood-hosted HSM).
- Determine tests that must pass in the private CI run (unit/plan/validate/integration smoke).
- Prepare a 1–2 page evidence summary for AegisBank security for Friday.

Attachments: priv-ci-checklist-v1.pdf, pipeline-diff.patch, helm-values-aegis.yaml

Notes: I think we can reuse the existing tf-module signing flow but need to confirm the signing key boundary for private deployments (customer-managed key may be required). Karthik — can you check the terraform module signing script and the way the pipeline records build metadata? Irene — can you advise on what level of test matrix the security team will accept? Vanessa — schedule owner: can you confirm a short readiness call with Aegis for Thu 4/29?

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Engineering Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priv infra CI safety checklist and artifact provenance for AegisBank

Thanks, Stephanie. Quick reads and a couple of clarifying questions below.

Summary feedback:
- Checklist looks good overall; add explicit TF plan output signing and a short notarization step for Helm charts (chart provenance in Chart.yaml).
- For Ansible, include a deterministic artifact build step (pin roles/collections) and record versions in the provenance metadata.

Questions:
1) Do we require customer KMS to sign artifacts, or will a Redwood HSM-signed bundle plus a signed attestation be OK? AegisBank sometimes insists on customer-managed keys.
2) For the private CI runs that will execute inside the customer's cloud, what network egress is allowed? We should avoid public calls for artifact verification if their environment is fully air-gapped.

Technical notes: I ran the pipeline-diff locally — the signing stage looks straightforward, but we need to add a small step to emit the build metadata JSON (build_id, git_sha, builder_image, timestamp, signature). I'll attach a quick text stub (tf-module-aegis-signing.txt) to illustrate the expected fields.

Action items I can take this week:
- Draft a minimal provenance JSON schema we can commit to the repo.
- Add Helm chart provenance checks to the chart CI job.

Irene
Principal Infra Engineer

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 13:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priv infra CI safety checklist and artifact provenance for AegisBank

Looping in some practical checks we should implement in the TF/Helm/Ansible pipelines before handing off: 

Terraform:
- terraform fmt & validate (already present)
- terraform plan with backend-stub (no apply) and deterministic plan output -> sign plan binary/JSON
- run terratest-style smoke in a sandbox (small infra e2e) for module changes

Helm:
- chart lint + helm unittest + generate provenance entry in Chart.lock
- sign packaged chart with cosign and record signature in artifact store

Ansible:
- lock Galaxy roles/collections via requirements.txt.lock
- artifactize playbook into tarball, sign tarball, and verify signature in CI

CI mechanics & storage:
- Use an S3-compatible artifact store inside the customer's VPC (object keys namespaced by customer/deployment/commit).
- Signing options: allow customer KMS (preferred) or Redwood key with a signed attestation PEM + CA chain. Document both options.
- For air-gapped customers: we can run an offline verifier that consumes a provenance JSON + signature and validates locally. Add a small verifier binary to the repo.

Commands I tested locally:
- cosign sign --key k8s/cosign.key ./chart-0.1.2.tgz
- sha256sum plan.out > plan.out.sha256 && cosign sign-blob --key cosign.key --output-signature plan.out.sig plan.out

I'll open a PR today with the pipeline additions and a demo verifying step. Priyom — can you confirm the deployment job that will run inside the customer's account has the needed IAM role to write to the artifact bucket?

-karthik

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priv infra CI safety checklist and artifact provenance for AegisBank

Great progress — a couple of logistics notes: 

- Stephanie: I booked a 45-min readiness call with AegisBank (Julie + their security owner) for Thu 2027-04-29 10:00 AM PDT. Calendar invite sent.
- I'll draft the 1–2 page evidence packet after we lock on the list of checks (Irene/Karthik please flag any items that must be called out explicitly).
- For key management: propose we present both options but default to customer KMS for production rollouts. For pilot, Redwood-signed artifacts + attestations may be acceptable if customer signs an exception.

Small ask for the team: please add one-line acceptance criteria to each CI job in the PR (e.g., "plan signed", "chart signature present", "artifact uploaded to s3://aegis-private-artifacts/"). That will help me finalize the evidence doc.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Program Manager, Customer Deployments

From: Julie Murphy <julie.murphy@aegisbank.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: AegisBank Security <security@aegisbank.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priv infra CI safety checklist and artifact provenance for AegisBank

Stephanie — thanks for pulling this together. A few clarifications from our side after a quick read: 

- We strongly prefer customer-managed keys for production. For the pilot, a Redwood-signed bundle + signed attestation is acceptable provided the provenance JSON and signature are verifiable without contacting external services.
- The artifact store must be accessible from our VPC with restricted IAM. We will provide a short-lived role for the Redwood pipeline to write objects.
- Please include a short note in the evidence packet about the offline verification flow (we need to run verification inside our environment).

We appreciate the level of detail on the checklist. Looking forward to the readiness call on 4/29.

Julie Murphy
Director, Infrastructure Security
AegisBank
